scope.purpose: Protect the independently audited app membership from silent loss in repository book intake. This is a diagnostic baseline, not a material admission or publication declaration.

appEvidence.method: Read-only source, entrypoint, loader-order, source-guard and reader-text comparisons against the current app and its matching November 8 APK-input archive. Effective current readers were distinguished from historical embedded payloads before mapping their stable identities to repository book scopes.
limitations: The recorded evidence is a static source/archive snapshot. It does not establish an installed phone application, a released APK, a fresh browser session, or a remote content-pack runtime.

All 84 Arabic extended Quran identities were observed. Full commentary text was not independently compared across all 84; those units are explicitly identity-only. Separate audited Arabic overlay and Infitar comparisons do not upgrade the whole Arabic inventory to text-exact.

Exact ordinary text comparison covers 112 translated Quran packages and 1608 introduction/verse entries. Source-path, display and documented provenance normalization does not confer new translation approval.
Eleven Fatiha packets and Japanese Qiyamah are exact reader comparisons. Nineteen Ikhlas comparisons establish original paragraph and note text, not identical original credit-object schemas.
All 47 Arabic article bodies and semantic-role runs match. Sixteen article reference/anchor differences remain recorded in knownAppGaps; the book source already contains those restorations.

Current Seerah membership is only Arabic new-seerah001 through new-seerah003. All 331 body paragraphs and 389 semantic segments match with line-ending normalization, but 52 quotation segments lack the reference metadata present in the book projection (28 Quran and 24 Hadith). Embedded historical lecture readers are not current menu editions.
Repository sourceBindings pin the exact public reader/source bytes compared in this audit. They are not hashes of the app runtime payload and must not be described as proof of full app-byte equality.

Changes to any pinned app entrypoint, data, source carrier or consumer require renewed effective-reader verification. Matching these pins verifies the audited snapshot only; it cannot discover uninspected files or new content by itself.

No source review, human scholarly certification, Microsoft Word layout receipt or final visual acceptance is created by this baseline. Previously selected and currently published contents must remain separately reported.

exclusions.reason: Simplified Quran is a separate edition and is outside this extended-book membership baseline. Simplified Fatiha and Ikhlas are intentionally unavailable in the audited app.
Raw embedded supplemental-language entries can be gated or superseded. Only effective dedicated Fatiha, Ikhlas and Japanese Qiyamah scopes admitted by the inspected consumers are represented.
Ten inspected independent FINAL decisions require changes and do not establish eligible current readers; no French final disposition was established in the bounded audit.

Seven exact qualified model-review passes were found for en, fr, tr, id, ms, es and ru, but final root acceptance and deployment were not established in the inspected records. Persian requires revision; other locale passes were not established. These are not current app baseline units.
All nineteen translated author packages remain pending independent final review in the inspected records.
The historical standalone article was merged into current Arabic article 26. Its older translations are not translations of the current merged article and remain held.

The active new-adult consumer replaces the older list and enables only three Arabic chapters. Historical embedded readers, a closed 68-record restoration proposal, and off-app work products do not establish current app membership.
These families are outside this bounded article, extended Quran and current adult Seerah baseline. Their presence or absence is not assessed by the 277-unit total.
